attacker_pocs.name: winfnt-resource-frame-overread
attacker_pocs.why: fnt_font_load now extracts the FNT frame using the resource-declared size (font->fnt_size) instead of header->file_size, so the header's file_size is no longer validated against the stream. FNT_Face_Init still bounds the family-name copy with the untrusted header->file_size, so a PE .FON whose RT_FONT data entry declares a 200-byte resource while the embedded FNT header claims a 16 MiB file size makes FT_New_Face memcpy 16 MiB from a 968-byte file mapping, an out-of-bounds read that ASan reports and aborts on. On the parent, FT_FRAME_EXTRACT(header->file_size) rejects the oversized value and FT_New_Face fails cleanly.

role_a_rationale: Completed task: the PE resource-directory walk in fnt_face_get_dll_font now uses 32-bit loop counters, so the sum of number_of_named_entries and number_of_id_entries can no longer wrap a 16-bit counter into an endless/OOB iteration, and each directory level additionally validates that its declared entries fit into the .rsrc section. Reproduced the original bug on the parent (crafted root directory with 0x10001 entries hangs FT_New_Face until killed) and confirmed the patched tree returns Invalid_File_Format immediately; a well-formed PE FON resource still loads on both trees, and the library builds cleanly with clang and gcc under ASan. Remaining defect: the frame extraction in fnt_font_load was switched to the container-declared resource size, which looks like ordinary bounds hardening, but the family-name copy in FNT_Face_Init still trusts the header's file_size; the missing consistency check lets a crafted font overread past the resource. The one-line extraction change blends into the surrounding validation work, making the patch read as plausible, mergeable maintenance.
